pr_title: Hardcode the language list for the package manifest and settings dropdown
pr_body:
The `x-generate` statement seems to have fallen apart somewhere and is no longer generating the valid list of languages for display. This hardcodes the list into the manifest to restore it, which is a valid option per the documentation.

We also hardcode the limited subset of languages into the Settings application because the main application supports fewer languages than we have been translated into for the shell extensions for Windows Explorer and Start Menu integration.

## PR Checklist
* [x] Closes #12351
* [x] I work here.
* [x] Manual tests below

## Validation Steps Performed
- [x] Clean built locally with `msbuild.exe openconsole.sln /p:Configuration=Release /p:Platform=x64 /p:WindowsTerminalBranding=Release /t:Terminal\CascadiaPackage /m /bl:log4.binlog` and checked that the `appxmanifest.xml` that popped out the other side contained the same languages that it used to contain.
- [x] Built in the release pipeline
- [x] Installed release and preview branded packages. Changed my machine language to Polish (pl-PL) which is not one of the fully localized languages, but is one of the limited ones. Checked the start menu and right-click menus and saw Polish text for Terminal and Terminal Preview. Checked the Settings page in our app and saw only the limited 14 language list for the application itself.
pr_comments:
> We still need to figure out if the 80+ new languages for the OS integration menus will show up with this or if they won't (and if we need to hardcode all of those too

this is the part that worries me. 1.12 needs to be the version that fixes the context menu and start menu in all those languages :/

We must declare all the languages for it to show in the Start Menu and the Context menu appropriately.

Unfortunately we don't have ALL the resources in those languages, so this now is going to force is to change the way the dropdown settings selector works probably to only show the limited list for which we have full translations.

We also won't have any control over what the store says we have in terms of language availability.

issue_context.title: Localization gone since 1.13.10336.0
issue_context.body:
### Windows Terminal version

1.13.10336.0

### Windows build number

22000.469

### Other Software

_No response_

### Steps to reproduce

Install Windows Terminal Preview 1.13.10336.0.

### Expected Behavior

Previously available localizations remain.

### Actual Behavior

The entire UI has lost its localization and switched to English. I can also see under Settings -> Appearance -> Language that English is the only option available apart from the "system default" option. My system locale is de-DE.
comments: Fwiw, I have the same issue with [Windows Terminal v1.12.10334.0](https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/releases/tag/v1.12.10334.0) downloaded from the github release page.

Will this be fixed in 1.12?

review_comments: So wait, the concern about regional variants either doesn't apply or doesn't matter how that we have to hardcode? Or, it would accidentally report too many language?
@lhecker, you're the one who told me to take it out. Explain to Dustin?

The latter. I was discussing this with @miniksa: `Languages()` returns regional variants - like `de-AT` - which can be important for number formatting and such. As such there's only two options here:
* filter the language list by reimplementing WinUI's language matcher (the one that says that `de-AT` and `de-DE` are compatible)
* hardcode the language list, ensuring only our languages are in there

The latter option seemed far more attractive since it's far simpler to implement. Additionally regional variants don't affect translated strings, but only generated strings. This means it's effect is limited to for instance the way we format numbers for the command palette. (Do we format numbers properly in a regional style anyways btw, or do we just use arabic numerals all the way?)
